title: Differentiation logs
unit: IAL Pure Mathematics (P3) - unit inferred from file name

questions.question: Figure 3 shows the curve C with equation x = y e^(2y), y in R. Show that dy/dx = y/(x(1 + 2y)).
steps: Differentiate x with respect to y: dx/dy = e^(2y) + y(2e^(2y)) = e^(2y)(1 + 2y).
From x = y e^(2y), e^(2y) = x/y (for y not 0).

questions.question: Figure 3 shows the curve C with equation x = y e^(2y). Given that the straight line x = k cuts C at exactly two points, find the range of possible values for k.
steps: Let h(y) = y e^(2y). Then h'(y) = e^(2y)(1 + 2y), which is zero at y = -1/2.
h(-1/2) = (-1/2)e^(-1) = -1/(2e), the minimum value of x on the curve.
For y < -1/2, h decreases from 0 (as y tends to -infinity) to -1/(2e).
For y > -1/2, h increases from -1/(2e) to infinity, crossing zero at y = 0.
For -1/(2e) < k < 0 there are two solutions (one on each branch); k = -1/(2e) gives one, k = 0 gives one, and k > 0 gives one.

questions.question: Find, using calculus, the x coordinate of the stationary point on the curve with equation y = (2x + 5)e^(3x).
steps: Stationary point: set dy/dx = 0; e^(3x) is never zero, so 6x + 17 = 0.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows the curve C with equation y = f(x), where f(x) = (2x + 1)^3 e^(-4x). Show that f'(x) = A(2x + 1)^2(1 - 4x)e^(-4x), where A is a constant to be found.
Hence find the exact coordinates of the two stationary points on C, where f(x) = (2x + 1)^3 e^(-4x).
steps: Stationary points: (-1/2, 0) and (1/4, 27/(8e)), where 27/(8e) is approx 1.2416.

questions.question: The function g is defined by g(x) = 8f(x - 2), where f(x) = (2x + 1)^3 e^(-4x). Find the coordinates of the maximum stationary point on the curve y = g(x).
steps: The maximum of f is at x = 1/4 with value 27/(8e).
g(x) = 8f(x - 2) translates f by 2 in the positive x direction, so x - 2 = 1/4 gives x = 9/4.
The factor 8 stretches y values: g(9/4) = 8 x 27/(8e) = 27/e.

keywords: express x in terms of y
questions.question: The curve has equation y = log10(2x + 1). Express x in terms of y.
steps: Write the log in index form: 10^y = 2x + 1.

questions.question: Hence, giving your answer in terms of x, find dy/dx for y = log10(2x + 1).
steps: Use log10(u) = ln(u)/ln 10, so y = ln(2x + 1)/ln 10.
Check with part (a): dx/dy = (10^y ln 10)/2 = (2x + 1) ln 10 / 2, which gives the same result.

questions.question: The sprinter's velocity is modelled by v = 12 - e^(t - 10) - 12e^(-0.75t), t >= 0. Using calculus, find the sprinter's maximum velocity during the race.
questions.answer: Maximum v = 12 - 7 x 3^(1/7) x e^(-30/7), approx 11.89 m/s (at t = (40 + 8 ln 3)/7, approx 6.97 s)
steps: dv/dt is positive before this t and negative after, so it gives a maximum.

questions.question: The sprinter runs 100 m in T seconds, so that the integral from 0 to T of v dt = 100, where v = 12 - e^(t - 10) - 12e^(-0.75t). Show that T = (1/12)(116 - 16e^(-0.75T) + e^(T - 10) - e^(-10)).
questions.answer: Shown by integrating v and rearranging
steps: Integrate v: integral of 12 dt = 12t; integral of -e^(t - 10) dt = -e^(t - 10); integral of -12e^(-0.75t) dt = 16e^(-0.75t).
So the integral of v from 0 to T = [12t - e^(t - 10) + 16e^(-0.75t)] from 0 to T.

questions.question: The iteration T(n+1) = (1/12)(116 - 16e^(-0.75Tn) + e^(Tn - 10) - e^(-10)) with T1 = 10 is used to approximate T. Find, to 4 decimal places, (i) the value of T2 and (ii) the time taken by the sprinter to run the race, according to the model.
steps: The sequence converges, so the fixed point of the formula is the race time.
The time taken is T = 9.7293 seconds to 4 decimal places.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows the curve C with equation y = f(x), where f(x) = e^(-x^2)(2x^2 - 3)^2. Find the range of f.
steps: f(x) is a product of e^(-x^2) > 0 and a square, so f(x) >= 0.
f(x) = 0 when 2x^2 = 3, so the minimum value is 0.
At x = 0, f(0) = e^0 x (-3)^2 = 9, which is the highest peak in Figure 1.
The other turning points (x^2 = 7/2) give f = 16e^(-7/2), approx 0.483, which is lower than 9.

questions.question: Show that f'(x) = 2x(2x^2 - 3)e^(-x^2)(A - Bx^2), where A and B are constants to be found, for f(x) = e^(-x^2)(2x^2 - 3)^2.
steps: Product rule: f' = -2x e^(-x^2) u + e^(-x^2) (du/dx), with du/dx = 2(2x^2 - 3)(4x) = 8x(2x^2 - 3).

questions.question: Given that the line y = k, where k is a constant and k > 0, intersects the curve y = f(x) at exactly two distinct points, find the exact range of values of k.
steps: Turning points: x = 0 (f = 9, maximum), x = +/- sqrt(3/2) (f = 0, minimum), x = +/- sqrt(7/2) (f = 16e^(-7/2), maximum).
For 0 < k < 16e^(-7/2) the line cuts the curve at six points (three per side).
For k = 16e^(-7/2) there are four distinct points, and for k = 9 there is one point (x = 0).
For 16e^(-7/2) < k < 9 the line cuts only the central peak on each side, giving exactly two points.
For k > 9 there are no intersections.

questions.question: The curve C has equation y = ln(x^2 + k)/(x^2 + k), x in R, where k is a positive constant. Show that dy/dx = Ax(B - ln(x^2 + k))/(x^2 + k)^2, where A and B are constants to be found.
steps: Let w = x^2 + k, so y = (ln w)/w and dw/dx = 2x.
dy/dw = [(1/w) x w - ln w x 1]/w^2 = (1 - ln w)/w^2.
dy/dx = dy/dw x dw/dx = 2x(1 - ln w)/w^2.
Substitute w = x^2 + k: dy/dx = 2x(1 - ln(x^2 + k))/(x^2 + k)^2.

questions.question: Given that C has exactly three turning points, find the x coordinate of each of these points, giving your answer in terms of k where appropriate.
steps: dy/dx = 0 when x = 0 (from the factor x) or when B - ln(x^2 + k) = 0.
B - ln(x^2 + k) = 0 gives ln(x^2 + k) = 1, so x^2 + k = e.
So x^2 = e - k, giving x = +/- sqrt(e - k).
These two extra roots exist only if e - k > 0, and they must be distinct from x = 0.
So the three turning points have x = 0 and x = +/- sqrt(e - k).

questions.question: Given that C has exactly three turning points, find the upper limit to the value of k.
questions.answer: k < e (upper limit e, not attained)
steps: Three turning points need the extra roots x = +/- sqrt(e - k) to exist and be non-zero.
This needs e - k > 0, so k < e.
At k = e the extra points coincide with x = 0, giving only one turning point.
So the upper limit for k is e.

questions.question: A population of toads is modelled by N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1), t >= 0. Calculate the number of toads at the start of the study.
steps: The start of the study is t = 0.

questions.question: Using N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1), find the value of t when there are 420 toads in the population, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
According to the toad population model N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1), explain why the number of toads can never reach 500.
questions.answer: N = 450 - 450/(2e^(0.12t) + 1) < 450 for all t, so N never reaches 500
steps: Since 2E + 1 > 0, the term 450/(2E + 1) is positive, so N < 450 for all t.
As t tends to infinity, N tends to 450, which is below 500, so N never reaches 500.

questions.question: The curve y = f(x), where f(x) = (x - 2)^2 e^(3x), x in R, has a maximum turning point A and a minimum turning point at (2, 0). Use calculus to find the exact coordinates of A.
steps: Stationary points: x = 2 (the minimum at (2, 0)) and x = 4/3.
Sign check: f' goes from positive to negative at x = 4/3, so it is a maximum.

questions.question: Given that f(x) = k, where k is a constant, has at least two distinct roots, state the range of possible values for k, where f(x) = (x - 2)^2 e^(3x).
steps: From part (a), f is increasing for x < 4/3, decreasing between 4/3 and 2, and increasing after 2.
f tends to 0 as x tends to -infinity, has a maximum 4e^4/9 at x = 4/3, and a minimum 0 at x = 2.
For k > 4e^4/9 there is one root; for k = 4e^4/9 there are two (x = 4/3 and one beyond 2).
For 0 < k < 4e^4/9 there are three roots.
For k = 0 there is only x = 2, so k = 0 is excluded.

questions.question: The curve C has equation y = sqrt(3 + 4e^(x^2)), x >= 0. Find dy/dx in simplest form.

keywords: show x = alpha is a solution
questions.question: P with x coordinate alpha lies on C, and the tangent to C at P passes through the origin. Show that x = alpha is a solution of 4x^2 e^(x^2) - 4e^(x^2) - 3 = 0.
steps: Tangent at P passes through the origin, so its gradient is y/x.
So dy/dx = y/x at x = alpha: 4 alpha e^(alpha^2)/y = y/alpha.

questions.question: Hence show that alpha lies between 1 and 2, where alpha satisfies 4x^2 e^(x^2) - 4e^(x^2) - 3 = 0.
questions.answer: h(1) = -3 < 0 and h(2) = 12e^4 - 3 > 0, so alpha lies between 1 and 2
steps: Let h(x) = 4x^2 e^(x^2) - 4e^(x^2) - 3, which is continuous.
Sign change on [1, 2] means a root lies in (1, 2), so alpha is between 1 and 2.

questions.question: Show that the equation 4x^2 e^(x^2) - 4e^(x^2) - 3 = 0 can be written in the form x = (1/2)sqrt(4 + 3e^(-x^2)).
steps: Take the positive square root (x > 0): x = (1/2)sqrt(4 + 3e^(-x^2)).

questions.question: The iteration x(n+1) = (1/2)sqrt(4 + 3e^(-xn^2)) with x1 = 1 is used to find an approximation for alpha. Using this iteration, find to 4 decimal places (i) x_3 (the scanned paper shows x^3, read here as the third iterate) and (ii) alpha.
steps: Continue: x4 = 1.1062, x5 = 1.1048, x6 = 1.1051 (values converge slowly, oscillating about the root).
The iteration converges to the root, so alpha approx 1.1051 (to 4 decimal places, checked by substitution: g(1.10506) = 1.10506).

questions.question: The surface area A m^2 of a pond covered by duckweed at time t days is modelled by A = pq^t, where p and q are positive constants. Figure 1 shows the straight line through (0, 0.32) and (8, 0.56) for log10 A against t. Find, to 3 decimal places, the values of p and q.
steps: Take logs: log10 A = log10 p + t log10 q, a straight line with intercept log10 p and gradient log10 q.
Answer: p = 2.089 and q = 1.072, to 3 decimal places.

questions.question: Using A = pq^t with the values found in part (a), find the rate of increase of the surface area covered by duckweed, in m^2 per day, exactly 6 days after the start of the study, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
steps: Using the exact form: A = 10^(0.32 + 0.03t), so dA/dt = 0.03 ln(10) x 10^(0.32 + 0.03t).

questions.question: Figure 3 shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation y = f(x), where f(x) = x(x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2). Find f'(x).

The line l is the normal to the curve y = x(x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2) at O and meets the curve again at P, which lies in the 3rd quadrant. Show that the x coordinate of P is a solution of x = -(1/2)sqrt(16 + e^(x/2)).
steps: Normal at O has gradient 1/4, so l: y = x/4.
At P: x(x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2) = x/4; P is not O so divide by x: (x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2) = 1/4.
x^2 = (16 + e^(x/2))/4. P is in the 3rd quadrant, so x < 0 and x = -(1/2)sqrt(16 + e^(x/2)).

questions.question: Using the iteration x(n+1) = -(1/2)sqrt(16 + e^(x_n/2)) with x1 = -2, find to 4 decimal places (i) the value of x2 and (ii) the x coordinate of P.
steps: x4 = -2.0226 again, so the sequence has converged.
x coordinate of P = -2.0226 to 4 decimal places.
